title: py output contract factory + stream adaptor for typed responses
creator: Liam Chen
description: We need a reusable 'Response Contract Factory' that composes typed (pydantic/dataclass) output models with streaming adapters and retry-safe hydration. The goal is to provide ergonomic APIs for users to consume both single-shot and streaming LLM responses as typed Python objects while preserving safety, predictable retry semantics, and low overhead in the hot path. This work covers: 1) a factory that emits either Pydantic v2 models or frozen dataclasses based on a user-provided schema declaration, 2) a streaming adaptor that consumes token/chunk events (SSE/HTTP chunking) and yields hydrated models incrementally, 3) partial-hydration support (shape-first) so callers can access fields as they appear without blocking full validation, 4) idempotent replay markers to make client-side retries safe (avoid double side-effects in user callbacks), and 5) helpers for common patterns (union tolerance, versioned schema tags, safe-deserialize hooks). Note: this ticket focuses on API/implementation for the Python SDK; TypeScript and Go follow-ups will use the same contract concepts.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: ResponseContractFactory(schema, backend="pydantic"|"dataclass") with create(), stream() methods documented

Streaming: async for model in ResponseContractFactory.stream(resp): yields incremental hydrated objects (fields present as available) with no more than 0.5ms average overhead per chunk in microbenchmarks
Retries: each stream yields a stable idempotency token; replaying with same token must not result in duplicate user-level callbacks (test coverage)
Validation: full-validation can be opted-in or deferred; default is shape-tolerant shallow-hydration to avoid blocking application I/O
Compatibility: supports Pydantic v2 model construction and standard dataclasses; has clear migration guide and examples
Docs: design doc + examples (sync/async, backpressure-aware consumer pattern) added to SDK docs site
Tests: unit and integration tests covering partial-hydration, union fallback, replay semantics, and benchmarks are included in PR
technical_notes: Design: two-layer approach - lightweight event parser -> hydration pipeline. Parser produces typed events (field:set/value, meta:progress, end). Hydrator composes events into model state.
Hydration modes: 'shallow' (assign raw values, minimal coercion), 'strict' (full validation via pydantic/dataclass constructors), and 'safe' (validate only non-deferred fields)

Streaming model: use async generator that yields models as they cross validation thresholds. Provide backpressure by exposing a 'pause_threshold' param that applies a simple bounded queue to underlying socket read loop

Retry semantics: include a per-stream UUID and sequence numbers for chunks. On network retry, client replays unacknowledged chunks; hydrator detects duplicates and drops or replays idempotently depending on handler config

Performance: initial microbench shows ~0.08ms extra per 512-byte chunk on an m6i-standard CI runner. Aim to keep overhead <0.3ms on real-world median chunk sizes. Optimize by avoiding heavy pydantic instantiation in shallow mode.
Security: avoid eval/exec in custom deserializers; safe-deserialize hooks must run in try/except and not call untrusted code. Sensitive fields should support masks in partial view
Interop: output objects must provide .raw_json and .schema_version metadata fields for observability and future migrations
decisions: Use Pydantic v2 as the recommended default backend for typed models; dataclasses supported for lightweight users
Expose both sync and async streaming helpers; core implementation uses asyncio primitives and sync wrappers adapt to threading via a tiny threadpool
Default hydration mode is 'shallow' to prioritize responsiveness for streaming consumers; add explicit param to opt into strict validation
Retry idempotency token baked into ResponseMetadata; server-side cooperation not required for basic client-side replay detection
